note: The largest of the Summers County-run camping areas on Bluestone WMA, on the flats where Indian Creek meets the New River, off Mouth of Indian Creek Road near Forest Hill. Boat ramp; fire rings, some tables. CAVEATS: nobody has reported what size rig fits - sites are dirt pads reached by gravel county roads, so scout before bringing EKKO in; the area floods in high water and parts may flood more often during the ongoing Bluestone Dam work (DNR District 4, 304-256-6947, has gate-closure updates). --Claude  AWH 2026-10-11: kept, though we can't tell whether the sites suit RVs. Call (304) 466-7119 for info. --Claude
summary: Summers County's Parks & Rec page still names Mouth of Indian Creek among its four primitive Bluestone WMA campgrounds, $15/night/site (fees already manual, re-confirmed) and gives the season: changed season year_round:false -> May-November (water levels permitting). WV DNR's Bluestone WMA page also lists Mouth of Indian Creek among the 'Additional campsites along the Bluestone River ... provided by Summers County' and warns only that portions of the WMA may flood more often for 10 years of dam work; no official page reports Indian Creek closed (the dam-work closures are the state park's Old Mill and East Shore). Not stated: site count, facilities, booking (left derived). Note trimmed of the count/price/season/facility/booking restatements.
flags: Conflicting DNR pages: WV DNR's District 4 WMA page says under '51. Bluestone Lake' 'On the WMA: Camping is not permitted', while DNR's own Bluestone WMA page (https://wvdnr.gov/wma/bluestone) and Summers County both list Mouth of Indian Creek as a county-provided campsite area (same conflict as Bertha 14057, Cedar Branch 14062, Shanklin Ferry 14063).

No closure found: no county or DNR page mentions Mouth of Indian Creek being closed for the Bluestone Dam construction; DNR says only that 'Over the next 10 years, portions of Bluestone WMA may be flooded more frequently and for longer periods of time due to work being done on the Bluestone Dam.'
Criteria (already accepted by AWH 2026-10-11): no official page says whether a 23-ft motorhome fits; the county says only 'primitive camping only'.
